rationale.conceptual: Established DFT methods (PBE, pseudopotentials, geometry relaxation) are non-trivial but standard. The main challenge is correct implementation of parameters (cutoff, k‑points) and charge integration in Wigner–Seitz spheres rather than inventing new theory.
rationale.execution: Multi‑stage pipeline: three separate DFT runs (LiSi relaxation, Li and Si references) plus extraction of structural, energetic, and charge‑density data. Involves coordinating different cell sizes, k‑point meshes, and a fragile tooling setup (plane‑wave code, pseudopotentials).

difficulty.reasoning: Standard DFT study of LiSi using PBE-GGA; requires multi-part workflow (three material systems), careful parameter setup, and post-processing of charge density, but no novel algorithm.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small unit cells (max 32 atoms), plane‑wave cutoff 271.6 eV; runs on a single CPU in a few hours with modest RAM; no large external data.
